units.spine: Nothing here is arranged for buying and selling in quantity. The road passes close enough all the same.
Whoever keeps this place running does it on the side. No trade or craft here answers to a formal office.
The town has drawn in from its edges, and the ground beyond them now stands empty.
These are slow troubles, not sudden ones, and the town has room to work at them.
Past a certain point the town would no longer be the same place, and it is close to that point now.
The town's trouble does not arrive all at once. The town gives up a little more each season than the one before, and gets nothing back.
Breaking even, more or less, is how the town's year closes, and that gets watched closely.
What gets written down about trouble here is a small part of what actually happens, and no one here chooses which part it is.
On the terms it currently has, the town gets by, and the judgment falls on the terms, not on the town.
Less stands between the town and trouble than its size would suggest.
Nothing armed stands ready in the town beyond whoever picks up a tool when trouble comes.
What comes out of the wilds finds no one in the town whose job it is to answer it.
More goes on in the town than its watch keeps track of, and little of it stays hidden.
A careful eye notices first that the town keeps nothing spare.
No one in the town works magic, keeps an arrangement for it, or expects to need one.
Food is not something anybody in the town spares a thought for.
The road passes close enough to the town that the distance has never needed arguing about.
Warmholz amounts to a handful of roofs, and the ground beneath them is the reason there are any at all.
Ties to the places nearby run the same ordinary course they would anywhere settled, and none of them stands out as anything more.
One loose thread turns up on a close look at the town, the kind a single institution would be enough to tie off.
